name: ARN Smart Image Optimizer
author: arnsmart

sections.description:
ARN Smart Image Optimizer is a free WordPress plugin that converts your JPG and PNG images to WebP or AVIF on your own server and serves the smaller copies to visitors, while your original images stay untouched. New uploads are converted automatically in the background, every image size gets its own copy, and existing images are converted by a bulk job you can pause, resume or cancel. No account, no API key, no external service.

Large images are a common reason WordPress sites load slowly. Choose WebP or AVIF once, start one bulk job for the images you already have, and manage everything on one dashboard under ARN WebPix.

✨ Why Image Optimizer?

  • Originals stay untouched – copies go to uploads/arn-image-optimizer; your JPG and PNG files are never changed or replaced.
  • Ready in a minute – activate, open ARN WebPix and start the bulk conversion.
  • Visitors never wait – conversion never runs inside a visitor’s page request or the upload request; background work is scheduled only while there is work to do.
  • Safe by design – each copy is written to a temporary file first, a copy larger or older than its original is never served, and deleting an image deletes its copies.
  • Nothing leaves your server – local conversion with GD or ImageMagick; no account, API key, ARN server or image service.
  • One plugin, one screen – numbers, bulk job, settings, storage and maintenance on one dashboard; status and actions in the Media Library.

🖼️ WebP and AVIF conversion

WebP or AVIF copies of your JPG and PNG images, every image size included.

  • WebP or AVIF output: one format for the whole site; JPG, JPEG and PNG are converted, SVG files are skipped safely and other media types are only counted.
  • Every image size: the full image, the original WordPress keeps before scaling large uploads, and every generated size (thumbnails and srcset sizes) get their own copy.
  • Quality: WebP from 1 to 100 (default 82; higher means better quality and a larger file); AVIF at a fixed standard quality (60).
  • Server engines: WebP uses GD first and ImageMagick as fallback; AVIF uses ImageMagick first and GD (imageavif(), PHP 8.1 or later built with AVIF support) as fallback. A notice warns when the server lacks both GD and Imagick or cannot encode AVIF.
  • Transparency kept: PNG transparency carries over to the copy.
  • Memory guard: an image too large for the available PHP memory is reported instead of stopping the job.

⚡ Bulk conversion and automatic uploads

Convert existing images in one background job; new uploads follow on their own.

  • Bulk conversion job: converts all remaining eligible images in the background with live progress; pause, resume or cancel it, and it keeps running when you leave the page.
  • Convert on upload: new JPG and PNG uploads are converted a few seconds after WordPress saves them, so uploading stays fast; very large images finish in later background steps.
  • Batch size and time budget: 1 to 25 images per batch (default 10) and 5 to 120 seconds per batch (default 30) while the dashboard is open; background runs stay small (at most 5 images or 10 seconds per minute).
  • Missing copies completed automatically: after an update or a format change the library is rechecked and missing copies are made gently in the background.
  • Failure handling: an image is tried up to three times, then marked failed so the rest of the job finishes; retry it from the Media Library.
  • Low disk protection: nothing new is written while less than 5% of the disk is free.
  • Job history: last run, converted, remaining and failed counts and a list of recent jobs.

🚀 Faster pages with WebP and AVIF delivery

Serve the smaller copies on every page without server rules or .htaccess changes.

  • Whole-page delivery: every <img> and <source> on front-end pages (theme, page builder, widgets, post content) gets the copy address in src, srcset and the usual lazy-load attributes (data-src, data-srcset, data-lazy-src, data-lazy-srcset, data-original, data-large_image).
  • The right copy for each size: every srcset entry and thumbnail gets the copy of its own size, not the full-size image.
  • Only smaller, fresh copies: a copy is served only when it exists, is not older than its original and is smaller than it; otherwise the original address stays.
  • Convert on view: a page image without a copy is queued and converted in the background in small batches (up to 300 waiting files); a failed file waits 24 hours before another try.
  • Stays out of the way: wp-admin, AJAX, REST, feeds, embeds, sitemaps, the Customizer and page builder editors and previews (Elementor, Beaver Builder, Divi, Oxygen, Bricks, Thrive Architect, WPBakery) keep the original addresses; pages larger than 3 MB are left alone.
  • Skip an image: add data-no-webp to an <img> or <source> tag to keep its original address.

Copies are served by address, without a browser check: WebP works in every current major browser. After a bulk conversion, clear your page cache.

📁 Media Library status, actions and folders

See and control conversion where you manage your media.

  • Status column (list view): converted with the saving (for example “✓ WEBP · −64%” and the size before and after), partly converted, failed, skipped or not converted, with Convert, Complete and Retry buttons.
  • Grid badges: every JPG and PNG tile shows its status; a fresh upload is converted right away while the Media Library is open.
  • Media window details: a WebPix status card in the media window and on the attachment screen with View Image and Download links for the copy; a View WEBP (or AVIF) row action in the list.
  • Bulk actions: select up to 500 images and choose WebPix: convert or WebPix: regenerate copies; progress is shown on the dashboard.
  • Basic media folders: create, rename, move and delete folders and subfolders, drag media onto a folder or select media and click “Move here”, upload into the open folder, and pick a folder in the media window of the post editor and page builders. Folders are labels: no file moves, no URL changes.
  • Folder permissions: every user who can upload sees every folder; administrators change all folders, other users those they created. Deleting a folder keeps its media.

🧹 Storage, maintenance and safety

Keep the copies folder tidy and the numbers right.

  • Dashboard numbers: total media, convertible JPG and PNG images, converted and remaining images, a media inventory (JPG, PNG, SVG, other) and a conversion progress bar.
  • Storage report: disk space of the WebP and AVIF copies by format, plus obsolete copies and copies whose original is gone; checked once a day or now with “Check storage”.
  • Review and delete: untick what you want to keep, then delete only the selected copies; originals are never touched.
  • Maintenance tools: Refresh Stats, Recalculate Inventory (scan the media library again) and Clear Old Logs (this plugin’s log entries older than 30 days).
  • Protected files get no public copy: files of WooCommerce downloadable products, Easy Digital Downloads and review photos waiting for approval are never converted; developers can add folders with the arnsmimo_protected_folders filter.
  • Copies follow their image: deleting, moving or holding an image removes its copies; one site-wide lock keeps two batches from running at once.

🧩 Works with ARN Smart products

  • ARN Free AI screen: includes Settings → ARN Free AI, the shared AI connection screen of ARN Free plugins (WordPress AI on WordPress 7.0+, or your own API key for OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, DeepSeek, Kimi, xAI Grok, Mistral or an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, with model, usage and monthly limits). Image Optimizer itself sends no AI requests.
  • ARN Smart WebPix Pro: while WebPix Pro is active and licensed on the same site, Image Optimizer pauses itself (no conversion, delivery, Media Library column or folder panel) and says so on its dashboard; its data is kept and it continues when Pro is no longer active.
  • ARN Smart Vendix: review photos Vendix holds for approval are converted only after approval, and their copies are removed when they are held again.

🔒 Privacy, performance and your data

  • Images are converted on your own server; no image, file name or site data is sent to ARN Smart or any other service.
  • Front-end cost: one output buffer on HTML pages; conversion runs only in the background or from an open admin page.
  • Deactivation keeps settings, copies and folders; uninstall removes data only when you choose so (see the FAQ).
  • WordPress Multisite: every site keeps its own settings, tables, copies and uninstall choice.
  • The dashboard font, Poppins, is bundled under the SIL Open Font License 1.1 (assets/admin/fonts/OFL.txt), so admin screens load no external font.

⭐ Go further with ARN Smart WebPix Pro

ARN Smart WebPix Pro includes everything in Free and adds:

  • WebP and AVIF together, quality presets (Smallest, Balanced, High or custom) with an adjustable AVIF quality, and GIF, BMP, TIFF, PDF preview and WebM video sources.
  • A <picture> element with the original as fallback, CSS background and page-builder stylesheet images, LCP and image dimension tools, and folder, image and page exclusion rules.
  • A CDN address for copies with automatic purges (Cloudflare, Bunny, KeyCDN, Fastly or a signed webhook) and a weekly delivery health check.
  • Shrinking large uploads and recompressing JPEG originals, with a backup and one-click restore.
  • AI-powered Media AI: alt text, titles, captions, descriptions and file names suggested through the shared ARN Smart AI connection, applied after review, every change undoable.
  • Advanced media folders, replacing a file while keeping its address, and watermarks with a protected clean copy.
  • Cloud storage on Amazon S3, Cloudflare R2, Wasabi, DigitalOcean Spaces, Bunny Storage or any S3-compatible storage.
  • WP-CLI commands, health checks, a support file, license management, private Pro updates and priority support.

WebPix Pro imports the copies Image Optimizer already made instead of converting again. Image Optimizer stays fully usable on its own, without a WebPix Pro license.

🔗 More from ARN Smart

Free on WordPress.org, usable alone or together:

  • ARN Smart AI-Powered Site Utilities for Elementor – Elementor widgets, header & footer builder, SEO and schema.
  • ARN Smart AI-Powered Visitor Intent – visitor-intent capture, triggers, analytics and contact actions.
  • ARN Smart Duplicate Post & Content Toolkit – controlled draft preparation, duplication and find and replace.
  • ARN Smart URL Manager – short links, redirects, QR codes and local analytics.

Pro editions with more power and priority support: Vendix, Visioix, WebPix, Clonex, Linkix, SiteWatch, Contix and DualFix. Explore all products at ARN Smart.

External services

Image conversion, delivery and media folders run on your own server and use no external service.

ARN Free AI (Settings > ARN Free AI). The plugin bundles ARN Free AI, the shared AI settings screen of ARN Free plugins. ARN Smart Image Optimizer itself sends no images, no AI requests and no site data to any AI provider, and it does not contact any ARN server. Only when a site administrator chooses a provider on that screen and clicks “Test connection” (one short fixed test prompt, no site content) or “Load models” (the provider’s model list) is a request sent, with the administrator’s own API key, to that provider only, at that moment. The API key is stored encrypted in the WordPress database. No data is sent to any other provider.

  • OpenAI: https://openai.com/policies/terms-of-use , https://openai.com/policies/privacy-policy
  • Anthropic (Claude): https://www.anthropic.com/legal/commercial-terms , https://www.anthropic.com/legal/privacy
  • Google Gemini: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/terms , https://policies.google.com/privacy
  • DeepSeek: https://cdn.deepseek.com/policies/en-US/deepseek-terms-of-use.html , https://cdn.deepseek.com/policies/en-US/deepseek-privacy-policy.html
  • Moonshot AI (Kimi): https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/agreement/modeluse , https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/agreement/userprivacy
  • xAI (Grok): https://x.ai/legal/terms-of-service , https://x.ai/legal/privacy-policy
  • Mistral AI: https://legal.mistral.ai/terms , https://legal.mistral.ai/terms/privacy-policy
  • OpenAI-compatible endpoint: requests go to the address the administrator enters; that service’s own terms apply.

If WordPress AI is chosen instead, the test request goes through the provider connected in WordPress (Settings > Connectors) under that provider’s terms.
sections.installation:
1. In WordPress, go to Plugins → Add New, search for ARN Smart Image Optimizer, then install and activate it. You can also upload the ZIP under Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin.
  2. Open ARN WebPix in the admin menu. Under Optimization Settings, choose WebP or AVIF, set the WebP quality if you like, and save.
  3. Click Start Bulk Conversion to convert the images already in your Media Library. The job continues in the background; pause, resume or cancel it on the same screen.
  4. New JPG and PNG uploads are converted automatically while “Convert on upload” is on. Follow each image in Media → Library (list view) and clear your page cache once the bulk job has finished.
sections.faq:
Do I need ARN Smart WebPix Pro or a license key?

No. ARN Smart Image Optimizer is free, works on its own and needs no account, API key or license key; updates come from WordPress.org. WebPix Pro is optional and adds both formats together, <picture> delivery, CDN and cloud storage, Media AI and priority support.

Will it slow down my site?

No. Conversion never runs inside a visitor’s page request or the upload request: uploads, bulk jobs and missing copies are converted in the background in small steps with a time budget, which suits standard shared hosting. On the front end the plugin adds one output buffer to HTML pages and checks each image file once per request.

Does it work on WordPress Multisite?

Yes. Network activation prepares every site, new sites are prepared when they are added, each site keeps its own settings, tables, copies and uninstall choice, and a site deleted from the network takes its tables with it.

What happens to my data when I delete the plugin?

By default your settings, statistics, folders and copies are kept. To remove them, turn on “Delete plugin data on uninstall” on the dashboard before deleting the plugin; the copies in uploads/arn-image-optimizer are removed only if “Also delete the WebP/AVIF copies” is also on. Original images and data of other plugins are never removed. On Multisite every site follows its own choice. With “Delete plugin data on uninstall” on, the shared ARN Free AI settings, saved API keys and usage history of the sites where it is on are removed too, but only when no other installed ARN Free plugin (active or not) still uses them.

Does it send data to external services or AI?

No. The plugin sends no images or site data to ARN Smart or to any other service, and it makes no AI requests. The only outbound requests are the “Test connection” and “Load models” buttons of the shared Settings → ARN Free AI screen, sent to the AI provider an administrator chose, when the administrator clicks them (see External services).

Which formats are supported, and what does my server need?

JPG, JPEG and PNG images are converted to WebP or AVIF; SVG files are skipped and other media types are only counted. WebP needs GD with WebP support or ImageMagick with WebP; AVIF needs GD imageavif() (PHP 8.1 or later built with AVIF support) or ImageMagick with AVIF. The dashboard warns when the server cannot write the chosen format.

Are my original images changed?

No. Original images are never changed or replaced; the WebP or AVIF copies are stored separately in uploads/arn-image-optimizer, so switching the plugin off simply brings back the original addresses.

Can I convert the images already in my Media Library?

Yes. Click Start Bulk Conversion on the ARN WebPix dashboard, or select images in the Media Library list view and use the “WebPix: convert” bulk action (up to 500 at a time). “WebPix: regenerate copies” makes fresh copies after you change the quality.

Can I set the quality?

Yes, for WebP: from 1 to 100, 82 by default. AVIF copies use a fixed standard quality (60); adjustable AVIF quality and quality presets are part of WebPix Pro.

What happens if ARN Smart WebPix Pro is installed too?

Image Optimizer pauses itself while WebPix Pro is active and licensed on the same site, so only one optimizer works on your images. Its settings, copies and folders are kept, WebPix Pro can import the copies it already made, and Image Optimizer continues when Pro is no longer active.
sections.changelog:
2.0.2

  • Fixed: after an update from 1.0.x or 2.0.0 the library is checked again and the copies are made with their new names; the dashboard no longer counts images whose copies have the old names as converted.
  • Fixed: files of WooCommerce downloadable products, Easy Digital Downloads and review photos waiting for approval get no public WebP/AVIF copy; copies that earlier versions made of them are removed once.
  • Fixed: an image that another plugin holds for approval (ARN Vendix review photos) is not converted until it is approved; its copies are removed when it is held again or moved, also at its old address.
  • Fixed: an image that stops PHP every time is marked failed after three attempts, so the rest of the job finishes.
  • Fixed: a broken settings form no longer turns switches on or resets settings it did not send.
  • Fixed: requests with a list where one value belongs are refused with nothing changed; folder names keep backslashes; deleting a folder needs the confirmation the panel sends.
  • Fixed: the tables of a site deleted from a network are dropped with it.
  • Fixed: shared ARN Free AI 1.0.6: the retry message shows the real number of attempts; the screen updates after “Remove saved key” and “Clear usage history”; a key set in wp-config.php is not sent to a changed endpoint; reasoning models get no temperature setting; deleting a network site removes its usage table.
  • Tested with Elementor 4.4.1.

Earlier versions: changelog.txt
